svg.title: The adoption ladder: six rungs, each useful on its own
svg.desc: Six steps in two rows of three, each a thing a developer can do with SHarness without doing the others. The first row runs on any operating system with no kernel needed. Rung 0: write a policy for your tool, hash it, publish the hash with the release; no code, any language. Rung 1: check and hash policies in your own language, about sixty lines; the seven vectors must agree. Rung 2: read the contract: when SHARNESS_AI_POLICY_HASH is set, refuse secrets on the command line and say which policy you run under. The second row needs Linux, or a platform that provides the components. Rung 3: run under an enforcer: sharness-ai run, or translate the policy to the sandbox you already have. Rung 4: use a component client instead of a raw socket: talk to sharness.net or sharness.kms over mutual TLS. Rung 5: build or host a component in your language, against the standard and its vectors. Under the ladder, one line: the policy is the centre; a developer who stops at rung 0 has already made their tool's mandate reviewable.
svg.text: THE ADOPTION LADDER · EACH RUNG USEFUL ON ITS OWN
ANY OPERATING SYSTEM, ANY LANGUAGE · NO KERNEL NEEDED

g.text: 0 · write a policy for your tool
Say what it reads, writes, runs and connects to.
Hash it. Publish the hash with the release.
No code; the mandate is now reviewable.
1 · hash and check in your language
Canonical JSON, SHA-256, the shape check:
about sixty lines. The seven vectors must
hash to the same values.
2 · read the contract
SHARNESS_AI_POLICY_HASH
When it is set: refuse secrets on argv,
say which policy you run under.

svg.text: LINUX, OR A PLATFORM THAT PROVIDES THE COMPONENTS

g.text: 3 · run enforced
sharness-ai run, with the hash you published;
or policy translate into the sandbox you
already have, and read the gap it prints.
4 · use a component
A client for sharness.net or sharness.kms
over mutual TLS, instead of a raw socket
or a key file. Your process never sees the key.
5 · build or host one
A component in your language, against the
standard and its vectors; a row in the
registry once it passes and is reviewed.

svg.text: Each rung is useful without the next. The policy is the centre: a developer who stops at rung 0 has already made their
tool's mandate reviewable, in a form any enforcer on the matrix can take.
Proposed, 25 Oct 2026. Rungs 1 and 2 are runnable in Python; rung 3 is sharness-ai run (E03) and policy translate (E10); rungs 4 and 5 are the design.
